key_insight: Surfactant kinetics matters mainly through dynamic surface tension during droplet impact, with Surfynol 465 producing larger wetting coverage than Triton X-100 or SDS, especially at higher surfactant concentration.
engineering_relevance: For rough-surface wetting control, choosing a surfactant with favorable adsorption dynamics can improve liquid coverage and influence impact-spreading performance.
method: Experimental drop-impact tests on rough surfaces
Compared Triton X-100, SDS, and Surfynol 465
Varied surfactant concentration and Weber number to separate spreading and recession effects
evidence_signal: The abstract reports nearly identical coverage evolution below the CMC, but clear differences at 2× CMC and larger final coverage with Surfynol 465 across the roughness range.
watch_item: Results are experimental and specific to the tested rough surfaces and impact conditions, so surfactant choice may not transfer directly to other materials or time scales.
paper_title: Effect of surfactant kinetics on the wetting following the drop impact onto rough surfaces
